title: Predicting the end
hookLine: people have set dates, like the Millerites; Jesus said no one knows the hour

lines: A PREACHER WORKS OUT A DAY.
THE SUN GOES DOWN ON IT.
cards: A preacher named William Miller sat down with the book of Daniel and a lot of arithmetic, and worked out when Christ would return. People believed him, and among his followers a day was fixed.
They told their neighbors and waited. The day came, and the sun went down on it like any other. His followers gave what came next a name: the Great Disappointment.
Others have set dates too, and each one has come and gone. Yet the Gospels record Jesus saying something very plain about that day, plain enough for a sticky note.

teach.h: NOT THE ANGELS, BUT THE FATHER ONLY.
teach.b: First, the plain words. In Matthew, on the Mount of Olives, Jesus says: "But of that day and hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only." In Mark, the King James text adds, "neither the Son."
Christians explain that line in different ways, but the sentence is hard to miss: not you, not the angels. Second, the thief.

teach.h: LIKE A THIEF IN THE NIGHT.
teach.b: Paul tells the Thessalonians "the day of the Lord so cometh as a thief in the night." A thief doesn't send a schedule.

In Acts, when the disciples ask the risen Jesus whether he will now restore the kingdom to Israel, he answers: "It is not for you to know the times or the seasons, which the Father hath put in his own power."
Then he's taken up, and two men in white ask, "why stand ye gazing up into heaven?" Third, what to do instead: "Watch therefore: for ye know not what hour your Lord doth come."
Right after, Jesus tells of a servant left in charge of a household: "Blessed is that servant, whom his lord when he cometh shall find so doing." Doing what? His job, feeding the household on time.
Watching here isn't staring at the sky with a calculator.
It's being found at your work, faithful, whenever the knock comes. Fourth, fear. Date-setting can run on dread and on excitement, and both can pull people out of their ordinary lives.
Not knowing the hour sends attention back to this one: the people in the house, the work in front of you.

how: Churches that say the Nicene Creed confess that Christ will come again, and some Christians read Matthew 24 in Advent as a call to watchfulness rather than a timetable.

o: setting a date for Christ's return or the world's end
a prophet's warning that a city is about to fall
reading the stars to tell a person's own future

games.q: the day and the hour — tap the pairs.
p: how the day of the Lord comes
worked out a time, and it passed

s: Jesus gave his followers a date for the end
"of that day and hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only."
in Acts, the risen Jesus says the times are not for them to know
"It is not for you to know the times or the seasons."
in Matthew 24, the servant who is blessed is the one watching the sky
he's the one his lord finds "so doing": feeding the household in due season.

games.q: you're a disciple on the Mount of Olives. you've asked Jesus about the end. what does he tell you about the day and hour?
o: he names the season so you can be ready.
no one knows it, not the angels, but the Father only.
he gives you a date to pass on to the others.
games.why: "of that day and hour knoweth no man." then he tells of a servant blessed for being found at his work.

practice: Name one fear about the end, once and quietly, about the world or your own life: a diagnosis, a deadline, a headline.
Picture setting it down on a table beside you like a bag carried too long, and without arguing with it, bring your attention to this hour: the room, the sounds, the next ordinary thing you'll do.
If you pray, hand the fear over to God; if not, just leave it on the table.

wordCard.voice: Predicting the end. People have set dates, and the dates have passed. In the Gospels Jesus says of that day and hour, no one knows.

orig.note: Greek: hour, the set time. "of that day and hour knoweth no man", Matthew 24:36.

carryVoice: Your line: no one knows the hour. Not the angels, and not the date-setters. Same time tomorrow.
